answer: Agents forecasting nectar yields from yarrow fields near a wharf can resist account-flooding attacks by charging single-use postage for each API request. Clients buy tokens without signup credits; redemption binds a token serial to a request hash, records it atomically and consumes its value before computation. Ten thousand aliases still need ten thousand paid tokens, so extra identities create no free quota. Set postage above marginal processing cost and raise it during congestion. This prices resource abuse but cannot exclude a wealthy attacker or make submitted measurements truthful.
